events.title: Construction of the Golden Gate Bridge Begins
events.description: Construction officially began on the Golden Gate Bridge spanning the strait between San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean. The project was led by chief engineer Joseph Strauss, with major contributions from designers Leon Moisseiff, Charles Ellis, and Irving Morrow.
events.significance: The bridge opened in 1937 and was the longest suspension bridge main span in the world at the time. It became an iconic symbol of San Francisco and American engineering ambition during the Great Depression.

events.title: President Nixon Orders Development of the Space Shuttle
events.description: U.S. President Richard Nixon announced that NASA would develop a reusable space transportation system, which became the Space Shuttle program.
events.significance: The Space Shuttle program flew from 1981 to 2011, launched and serviced satellites, and helped build the International Space Station, shaping human spaceflight for three decades.

events.title: Founding of the German Workers' Party
events.description: Anton Drexler and others founded the German Workers' Party (DAP) in Munich. Adolf Hitler joined later that year and the party was renamed the National Socialist German Workers' Party (Nazi Party) in 1920.
events.significance: The party grew into the Nazi Party, which took power in Germany in 1933 and led the country into World War II and the Holocaust.

events.title: Founding of the Khmer Rouge's Democratic Kampuchea Constitution
events.description: Cambodia's Khmer Rouge regime proclaimed a new constitution renaming the country Democratic Kampuchea, formalizing the government under Pol Pot's leadership.
events.significance: The regime was responsible for the Cambodian genocide, in which an estimated 1.5 to 2 million people died from execution, forced labor, starvation, and disease before its fall in 1979.

events.title: Nellie Tayloe Ross Sworn In as First Female U.S. State Governor
events.description: Nellie Tayloe Ross became governor of Wyoming after winning a special election following the death of her husband, Governor William B. Ross. She took office on January 5, 1925.
events.significance: Ross became the first woman to serve as a governor of a U.S. state, a milestone for women's political participation, and she later served as the first female director of the U.S. Mint.
